chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ẓarīf, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
When a woman reaches fifty years, she does not see redness, unless she is a woman from Quraysh.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the female subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.حُمْرَةً: redness; referring here to menstrual bleeding
key_terms.خَمْسِينَ: fifty; the age threshold mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.سَنَةً: year; the unit of age in the ruling
key_terms.قُرَيْشٍ: Quraysh; the tribal exception mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: At what age is menstrual blood no longer recognized for a woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the age at which menstrual blood is no longer considered for a woman. It states that after fifty years, a woman does not see menstrual blood, except in the case of a woman from Quraysh.
